| [THEORY-028](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-028.md) v2 | Generalisation error ≤ √(2σ²·I) | Russo & Zou (2015), [LIT-356](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-356.md), Prop. 1: \|E[φ_T − µ_T]\| ≤ σ√(2·I(T;φ)) for any selection T among σ-sub-Gaussian statistics. Xu & Raginsky (2017), [LIT-347](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-347.md), Thm 1: \|gen\| ≤ √(2σ²·I(S;W)/n) for any algorithm P_{W\|S}. Both proofs rest on Donsker–Varadhan and were checked by the readers. The bound is in expectation only. It is vacuous for deterministic learners on continuous hypotheses, where I(S;W) is infinite, and for any real network when I is bounded by counting bits. It is tight only for Gaussian argmax and threshold selection. | Active |
| [THEORY-031](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-031.md) v2 | Detection criteria differ only in threshold | Peterson & Birdsall (1953), [LIT-364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-364.md) — the threshold on ℓ = f_SN/f_N is optimal for expected value and at fixed false-alarm rate, and the two optimum families coincide (Part I Thms 1–7). The ROC's slope equals the threshold (Thm 8). Tanner & Swets (1954), [LIT-368](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-368.md), carry this over to the human observer as d′ plus a criterion. Stanislaw & Todorov (1999), [LIT-367](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-367.md), state that d′ varies with the criterion unless the variances are equal. The separation of sensitivity from bias is a property of the model, not of the data. | Active |
| [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md) | Markov blankets exist around almost any set | The formal core of Bruineberg et al.'s critique ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md), C4 in [NOTE-447](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-447.md)). In a directed acyclic graph the blanket of a node set A is its parents, children and the children's other parents, and A is conditionally independent of everything outside A and its blanket. That holds for every A, so any set whose blanket leaves something outside gets a valid internal, blanket and external partition. Having a blanket therefore picks out no set. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the set was picked by spectral clustering with k = 8, not by the blanket. Active because it is a short derivation that anyone can check. It covers graphical (Pearl) blankets and the 2013 procedure. It does not cover the later sparse-coupling definitions at nonequilibrium steady state, which the record has not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-068](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md) v2 | Leaky accumulators optimal only when balanced | Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md)) prove that the pure drift diffusion model is the continuum limit of the sequential probability ratio test, and so the optimal two-choice decider, and that the linearised Usher–McClelland network reduces to it exactly when leak equals inhibition (and, for free response, when both are also large). Usher and McClelland ([LIT-565](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-565.md)) derived the difference of the two units as an Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process with net leak K = k − β: K ≠ 0 caps accuracy, leak-dominant weights late evidence and inhibition-dominant early. Active because the core is derivation, checkable on paper. What it does not say: that brains are balanced, that the result carries to more than two options or to non-stationary evidence, or that the primacy and recency seen in six participants are explained by it. | Active |
| [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) v3 | Blanket placement is fixed by prior modelling | Bruineberg et al. ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md)) and Raja et al. ([LIT-598](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-598.md)) argue, by different routes, that the Markov blanket of the free-energy literature is placed and not found. The formal core is [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md): the partition takes the internal set as input. This account adds what the critiques show about practice. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the graph was built from one kind of coupling and steady state was assumed when the run stopped. In published applications the blanket sits wherever the model needs it: in the receptors of a brain, the membrane of a bacillus, the beam joining two pendulums. The formalism also gives the same description to a membrane the cell makes and a beam nobody's states make. So the blanket presupposes the boundary it is offered as the criterion of. Active since 2026-10-27, narrowed to the 2013 formulation and the applications held. The later steady-state definitions have not been read, and the unrestricted claim is THEORY-1097, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-079](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-079.md) v3 | Laplace BMR misprices singular reductions | The filer's synthesis, stated by no source. BMR's closed form (Friston & Penny, [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 9; Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), Eq. 11) charges a reduction through log-determinants of Gaussian precisions, which is MacKay's regular Occam factor. Watanabe, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), says that models with hierarchical layers or hidden variables are singular, that no normal distribution approximates their posterior, and that their free energy grows as λ log n. BMR is applied to exactly such models: mixtures, hierarchical empirical Bayes and latent states. Neither literature cites the other. The exact identity is untouched ([THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md)). The claim is about its Laplace form, and a test on reduced-rank regression would settle it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-081](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-081.md) v2 | Reduced-model evidence is a prior-ratio average | Friston & Penny (2011), [LIT-620](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-620.md), Eq. 3: if models share a likelihood and differ only in priors nested inside a full prior, then p(y\|m_i) = p(y\|m_F)·E_{p(θ\|y,m_F)}[p_i(θ)/p_F(θ)]. Their Eq. 6 is the point-mass case, the Savage–Dickey ratio that Wagenmakers et al. (2010), [LIT-609](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-609.md), derive from the other end, and that Dickey (1971), LIT-610, stated in this form for any continuous likelihood. Friston, Parr & Zeidman, [LIT-614](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-614.md), restate it for any new prior and give conjugate closed forms. Active because the identity is three lines of Bayes' rule that anyone can check. The two Savage–Dickey conditions turn out to be the same condition. The identity is exact. Its Laplace and variational forms are only as good as the full posterior, and with no constraint on the prior family the optimum is maximum likelihood. | Active |
| [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md) v4 | Singular models pay λ log n, below d/2 | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), writes the evidence as best-fit likelihood times an Occam factor, the ratio of posterior to prior accessible volume, which under a Gaussian approximation is P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A. When the likelihood dominates, det A grows as n^d, so the penalty is (d/2) log n. Watanabe's WBIC paper, [LIT-616](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-616.md), recovers that case (Lemma 3, Theorem 5) and states what replaces it when the Fisher information is degenerate at the optimum: λ log n − (m − 1) log log n, with λ the RLCT (Theorem 2). The regular half is re-derived by Laplace's method with its conditions. The singular half is Watanabe's cited theorem, checked by exact free energies in two singular models of known λ. The volume reading of λ is in Watanabe's book, which is unread. | Active |
| [THEORY-155](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-155.md) v3 | Bayesian iterated learning converges to the prior | Griffiths & Kalish (2007), [LIT-769](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-769.md), read in [NOTE-599](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-599.md): a chain of learners who share a prior and each sample a hypothesis from their posterior is a Gibbs sampler, so the probability a learner holds a hypothesis converges to its prior probability, whatever the amount of data passed on; with MAP learners the outcome centres on the prior's mode but depends on data amount and noise, and can amplify weak biases. It is a theorem about an idealized chain. It does not say human chains reach the prior, and Kirby, Cornish & Smith's laboratory chains, [LIT-771](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-771.md), are consistent with it without testing it. Whether human chains do is [QUESTION-137](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-137.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-157](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-157.md) | Sufficiency theorems hold in Markov categories | Fritz (2020), [LIT-772](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-772.md), read in [NOTE-588](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-588.md), Theorems 14.5, 15.8 and 16.3 with the definitions of Sections 13–15. Sufficiency, completeness and ancillarity are stated with copy, discard, composition and almost-sure equality alone. Basu's theorem follows with no further axiom; Fisher–Neyman and Bahadur use strict positivity, which Stoch has although it lacks regular conditionals. The match with the classical theorems is shown in FinStoch (Fisher–Neyman) and through bounded completeness in Stoch (Basu), not for measure-theoretic Fisher–Neyman. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-158](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-158.md) v4 | Conserved mean alone doesn't give a symmetry | Baez & Fong (2013), [LIT-773](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-773.md), read in [NOTE-598](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-598.md): Theorem 1 (finite state space, four equivalent conditions), which the record re-derived. Theorems 2–3 (σ-finite measure spaces, without the component form) are reported as the source's (QUESTION-144). Unlike quantum mechanics, where a mean conserved in every state already implies commutation, a Markov process can conserve the mean of an observable it does not commute with. The theorem covers diagonal observables only; it says nothing about symmetries that permute states. | Active |
| [THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md) v4 | Question-order equality doesn't favour quantum | Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin & Busemeyer (2014), [LIT-795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-795.md), on the QQ equality derived in [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md): across the 66 Pew surveys of 2001-2011 that varied the order of two questions, question order shifts the answers (p = 0.0004) but not the probability that the two answers agree (p = 0.4625). The Lüders projection model predicts this without parameters, by a one-line identity. A classical model with order events can be built to satisfy the equality, and [LIT-264](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-264.md) shows that data meeting it are noncontextual, so it is evidence for a constraint on order effects, not for nonclassical probability or contextuality. A preregistered test with a constrained classical rival is [QUESTION-210](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-210.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md) v5 | Listeners infer speakers choose by informativeness | Frank & Goodman (2012), [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md), read in [NOTE-634](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-634.md): a parameter-free Bayesian listener inverting a size-principle speaker, with a separately measured salience prior, matches mean listener bets over seven context types at r = .99 (.87 without the 0 and 100 predictions), while salience alone correlates at r = .19. | [THEORY-177](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-177.md) v2 | CbD signalling is twice least context influence | Wang, Sadrzadeh, Abramsky & Cervantes (2021), [LIT-851](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-851.md), Proposition 1. | [THEORY-215](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-215.md) | Subcritical Hawkes processes are stationary | Brémaud and Massoulié (1996), [LIT-1035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1035.md), read in [NOTE-728](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-728.md): Theorems 1, 2, 7 and 8, proved. Inhibition is allowed because the conditions use \|h\|. The conditions are sufficient, not necessary; the kernels are fixed in time; uniqueness is among solutions with finite mean intensity. In the linear excitatory case the condition is the branching ratio below one, but in the nonlinear signed case the spectral-radius quantity is a bound, not a branching ratio, and a bounded rate needs no bound on the kernels at all. Nothing is proved about cascade sizes or about what happens past the threshold. | Active |
| [THEORY-247](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-247.md) v3 | Bisimulation metric is optimal transport | Calo, Jonsson, Neu, Schwartz & Segovia-Aguas (2024), [LIT-962](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-962.md), read in [NOTE-757](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-757.md). For finite action-free chains with real labels r and discount γ, the bisimulation metric's fixed-point equation is the Bellman equation of transport over bicausal couplings with cost (1−γ)\|r(x)−r(y)\|, so the two coincide. The transport cost equals 1/(1−γ) times the minimum of a linear objective over occupancy couplings, under flow and coherence constraints (Lemma 1, Theorem 1). It says nothing of systems with actions. Its link to trace distance is one-way and second-hand. | Active |
| [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) v4 | Transformers embed factored states orthogonally | Shai et al. (2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md). The lossless embedding is an elementary theorem (Prop. 2.2, Thm 2.3, App. A). The rest is experiment on five synthetic factors: about 10 effective dimensions against 242 for the joint state, approximate orthogonality in the first two components, and under token noise a collapse to the factored form before expansion. It does not show that the preference is architectural rather than a feature of training, a question the paper leaves open, and it varies neither the objective nor the data domain. | Active |
| [THEORY-280](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-280.md) v3 | Bisimulation metric estimable without a model | Calo, Jonsson, Neu, Schwartz & Segovia-Aguas (2025), [LIT-948](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-948.md), read in [NOTE-763](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-763.md). Bicausal occupancy couplings are characterised by constraints that use only each chain's sampled occupancy measure over consecutive state pairs. A stochastic primal-dual method on them gets an ε-accurate estimate with probability 1−δ from O((\|X\|\|Y\|(\|X\|+\|Y\|) + (\|X\|+\|Y\|)log(1/δ))/((1−γ)²ε²)) independent samples per chain. The states must be observed and enumerable, the cost known, and the samples drawn with restarts. A single running stream and latent states are outside it. | Active |
| [THEORY-289](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-289.md) v3 | Keeping data bounds model-collapse error | Gerstgrasser, Schaeffer, Dey et al. (2024), [LIT-971](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-971.md), read in [NOTE-815](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-815.md), Theorems 1–2 extending Dohmatob et al.'s replace result. Proved for ridgeless OLS with isotropic Gaussian features, the real covariates reused every round and only labels regenerated. The error is bounded, not constant: it rises every round towards its limit, and every model remains a noisier copy of the first. Small language and diffusion models behave alike over five to eight rounds; a VAE's error still rises. | Active |
| [THEORY-305](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-305.md) v2 | InfoNCE isn't spectral clustering proper | Tan, Zhang, Yang & Yuan (2023, ICLR 2024), [LIT-227](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-227.md), read in [NOTE-846](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-846.md): Theorem 3.1 and its proof (App. A), Lemma 2.5 and Definition 2.7. | [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) v4 | Small-batch class counts hurt joint-embedding SSL | Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), §§3–5 and Appendix C, read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md). The prior is explicit in MSN's loss (a KL to uniform over mean cluster assignments) and in SwAV's equipartition constraint. For VICReg it rests on an informal reduction of a simplified loss to K-means and on K-means's cited tendency to equal clusters, and for SimCLR on a cited equivalence, so the title claims the prior for MSN and SwAV only. | [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) v4 | Kernel quantum relative entropy lower-bounds KL | Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md). Σ_p = ∫ϕϕ* dp is uncentred and unit-trace, so p ↦ Σ_p maps distributions to quantum states, and D(p̃‖q̃) ≤ D(Σ_p‖Σ_q) ≤ D(p‖q) (Proposition 4(d), Eq. 8). The upper bound is joint convexity, with equality for every pair only if k(x,y) = 0 for x ≠ y. The lower bound is monotonicity under a measurement whose outcome law is p smoothed by h(x,y) = ⟨ϕ(x), Σ^{−1/2}ϕ(y)⟩². The O(σ²) gap is shown only for kernels on the torus with Fourier coefficients proportional to e^(−σ‖ω‖₁), with Lipschitz densities. It does not cover centred kernels, or similarity measures that compare Gram matrices of representations. | Active |
| [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) v2 | Ideal-observer stages locate perceptual losses | Geisler (2011), [LIT-1055](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1055.md), read in [NOTE-870](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-870.md). A review that defines the ideal observer as optimal "given the available information and any specified constraints", and writes it as an expected-utility argmax over the posterior given the stimulus S or a constrained representation Z = g(S;θ). Constraints are added one at a time (optics, receptor sampling and noise, ganglion-cell summation), and human performance that parallels the retinal-stage ideal while falling below it is read as loss in central factors. The empirical parts are the review's account of studies the record has not read. The review gives no formula for efficiency and no notion of an optimum over a restricted class of computations. | Active |
| [THEORY-339](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-339.md) | Probability judgments reuse earlier answers | Dasgupta, Schulz, Goodman and Gershman (2018), [LIT-1074](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1074.md), read in [NOTE-875](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-875.md); Gershman and Goodman (2014), [LIT-1056](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1056.md), read in [NOTE-886](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-886.md); Dasgupta and Gershman (2021), [LIT-1077](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1077.md), read in [NOTE-865](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-865.md). In five small online experiments, an earlier answer shapes a later one only when the later query can use it, and errors in the first carry into the second. The authors call this amortized inference, reuse of past computation bought at a cost in bias. The speed benefit is shown once (median log-RT facilitation, n ≈ 50 per order) and otherwise assumed; storage and retrieval are free in the models; the 2021 review adds stale cached values from the planning literature, second-hand. No paper prices when reuse pays or touches stores outside the head. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-349](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-349.md) | OI to bounded tests is multicalibration | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md), and Hébert-Johnson, Kim, Reingold and Rothblum (2018), [LIT-1052](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1052.md), read in [NOTE-879](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-879.md). A predictor is outcome indistinguishable relative to a class of distinguishers when none can tell nature's outcomes from outcomes drawn from the predictor, up to ε. With no access or sample access to the predictor this is equivalent to multi-accuracy or multicalibration over closely related classes, and a predictor meeting it exists at size O(s/ε²) (O(s/α⁴γ) for multicalibration), independent of nature. Learning a multicalibrated predictor is equivalent to weak agnostic learning of the class. Adequacy here is relative to the class, the outcome and the features, and is not unique; it is not closeness to the truth, and the papers say nothing about signal detection. | Active |
| [THEORY-354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-354.md) v2 | Refutation power depends on access to predictor | Dwork, Kim, Reingold, Rothblum and Yona (2021), [LIT-1068](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1068.md), read in [NOTE-885](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-885.md). Against sample-access distinguishers of size s an outcome-indistinguishable predictor of size O(s/ε²) always exists. Against oracle-access distinguishers, under fine-grained hardness of clique counting or BPP ≠ PSPACE, there are natures and polynomially many cheap distinguishers such that no predictor much cheaper than nature is indistinguishable. Non-adaptive queries add little; the power comes from adaptive queries. The results are conditional and asymptotic, with upper and lower bounds in different parameterisations; they say nothing about human observers or about which access a real auditor has. | Active |
| [THEORY-366](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-366.md) | Concentrated distances make nearest ≈ farthest | Beyer, Goldstein, Ramakrishnan and Shaft (1999), [LIT-1099](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1099.md), read in [NOTE-917](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-917.md) from the authors' 1998 technical report. Theorem 1: for n fixed data points and an independent query, var(d^p / E[d^p]) → 0 implies P[DMAX ≤ (1+ε)DMIN] → 1 for every ε > 0. The index m is arbitrary, so dimension enters only through the workload's distance distributions. IID coordinates and several correlated or non-identical workloads satisfy the condition; a diagonal line, two latent degrees of freedom and queries inside clusters do not. The condition is sufficient, not necessary. The result concerns the ratio of distances at fixed n, and does not show that real high-dimensional data loses contrast, or that indexes fail. | Active |
| [THEORY-378](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-378.md) | Uniform refresh beats proportional refresh | Cho and Garcia-Molina (2000), [LIT-1119](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1119.md), read in [NOTE-906](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-906.md). Freshness is the fraction of items equal to their source, age the mean time since an unseen change, both averaged over time and over equally weighted items. With fixed-interval refresh, uniform refresh is never worse than proportional on either measure, by convexity (proof in the authors' technical report). Under a fixed budget the freshness-optimal allocation starves the fastest-changing items; the age-optimal one refreshes them somewhat more. It prices staleness as an objective under a fixed budget: there are no reads, no query savings, no build cost and no cost of a stale use, so it is a staleness term and not a model trading staleness against upkeep. | Active |
| [THEORY-405](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-405.md) v2 | Summed guidance composes concepts, not relations | Liu, Li, Du, Torralba & Tenenbaum (2022), [LIT-770](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-770.md), read in [NOTE-597](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-597.md). CLEVR object positions, 1/2/3 components: 86.42/59.20/31.36% against an EBM's 70.54/28.22/7.34%. Relations: 60.40/21.84/2.80% against 78.14/24.16/4.26%. FFHQ attributes are comparable to LACE. Text-model composition (GLIDE, Stable Diffusion) is shown only in figures, with attribute confusion and hybrid objects among its listed failures. The product is derived at the data distribution and applied at every noise level, which [NOTE-597](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-597.md) notes is in general not the score of the noised product. | Active |
| [THEORY-419](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-419.md) v3 | Observational equivalence leaves effects open | Pearl (2009), [LIT-894](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-894.md), skimmed in [NOTE-696](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-696.md) from four excerpts the author posts: the contents, the second-edition preface, §§5.3.2–5.4.1 and the Epilogue, 46 of some 480 pages.
