The surgery needs autonomous equations and a diagram saying which equation belongs to which variable. The excerpts state the three rules of the do-calculus without derivation, and contain no three-level hierarchy of association, intervention and counterfactual. | Active |
| [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md) v2 | Recursive EFE prunes plans as a tree search | Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp & Parr (2020), [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md), read in [NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md) as prose: the equations were not recoverable from the text layer. The recursion is a construction (strong). That it plans through costs rests on single deterministic runs of a T-maze and an 8 × 8 maze. The title keeps that scope. Active as a report of the construction and of those runs; the general form is THEORY-1245, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-455](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-455.md) | Quantum formalism fits indivisible stochastics | Barandes (2023), [LIT-086](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-086.md), read in full in [NOTE-080](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-080.md). Γ_ij = \|Θ_ij\|² = tr(Θ†P_iΘP_j) is an identity (Θ_ij = √Γ_ij works), and a unitary Θ on the original space exists only for doubly stochastic Γ. Interference is the cross-term of Eq. 43 against a would-be Markov factorization, and a perfectly correlating environment that then evolves separately makes the process divisible (Eqs. 45–56). The "emergent" Schrödinger equation is the definition of H, unitarity is a choice the claimed gauge freedom does not preserve, and the decomposition is relative to a configuration basis the paper never fixes. | Active |
| [THEORY-472](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md) v4 | Size principle follows from informative speech | Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md), read in full in [NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md). The derivation (utility −D_KL from intended to literal meaning gives P(w) ∝ \|w\|^(−α) for a point referent) is a proof under its assumptions. Learners' bets track the parameter-free inversion at r = .93 on condition means (700 web participants); speakers' tag-word use in free descriptions correlates at r = .19, .51 without colour terms and .02 for them. In these displays the informative-speaker learner and a plain size-principle learner coincide by construction, so the fit does not show that learners reason about the speaker. | Active |
| [THEORY-475](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-475.md) | Hierarchical Bayes recovers DDM parameters best | Wiecki, Sofer & Frank (2013), [LIT-563](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-563.md), read in [NOTE-466](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-466.md). Experiment 1 gives the lowest trimmed recovery error for HB on every parameter, and HB beat ML on the same data sets in every condition. Experiments 2–3 report more power to detect drift differences and trial-wise covariate effects, but HB was judged by a posterior-interval test and the others by t-tests, and the clean comparison was omitted. All data were generated from DDMs, with sz = st = 0. It is the standard partial-pooling result shown for one model family, not a test of the DDM. | Active |
| [THEORY-489](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-489.md) | Iterated learners converge to positive linear | Kalish, Griffiths & Lewandowsky (2007), [LIT-820](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-820.md), read in [NOTE-616](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-616.md). 288 participants in 32 nine-generation chains, four starting conditions. 28 families converged to a positive linear function; 3 converged to the negative linear one and 1 had not converged. The bias was taken from earlier studies, not measured on these learners, and stationarity was not established. It supports the claim that human transmission chains settle on what learners favour in this task, not that they reach the Bayesian prior, and it cannot tell sampling learners from MAP learners. | Active |
| [THEORY-515](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-515.md) v2 | Joint-space Schrödinger bridges sample posteriors | Shi, De Bortoli, Deligiannidis & Doucet (2022), [LIT-776](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-776.md), read in [NOTE-589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md). Propositions 1–3 are proofs, read for structure and not checked line by line. The empirical gains over the conditional score model hold at equal, small step counts on most but not all image metrics, and in Lorenz-63 filtering at 20 steps. That a long noising horizon is not what makes conditional diffusion correct is [NOTE-589](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-589.md)'s interpretation, not something the paper tests. | Active |
| [THEORY-534](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-534.md) | ML optimality was never one theorem | Stigler (2007), [LIT-044](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-044.md), read in full in [NOTE-074](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-074.md). Fisher's 1922 proof rests on sufficiency, his 1925 proof on exact normality, and his private 1930 proof on multinomial data and smooth degree-0 estimators. Rigorous treatments (Wald 1943, Cramér 1946) came at the cost of unwieldy conditions. Neyman–Scott, where the MLE of σ² tends to σ²/2, is the failure Stigler weighs as practical; Hodges's superefficiency is possible only on a Lebesgue-null set (Le Cam 1953). It is a history: the theorem statements are reconstructions, and it says nothing about modern overparameterized models beyond one hedged warning. | Active |
| [THEORY-542](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-542.md) | Inferring speaker intent improves word learning | Frank, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-815.md), read in [NOTE-611](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-611.md). On about twenty minutes of video from two dyads, annotated by the authors, the intentional model's lexicon scores precision .67 and F .55 against .06–.15 and .10–.22 for five baselines. The behavioural fits are qualitative, the baselines also produce mutual exclusivity, and the Baldwin case supplies the intention rather than inferring it. The reading said no THEORY, because the findings are specific to a small corpus and the record held nothing they correct; this account is filed Proposed for that reason. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-545](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-545.md) | Quantum concept model is classical underneath | Aerts & Gabora (2005), Parts II and I, [LIT-312](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-312.md) and [LIT-340](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-340.md), read in [NOTE-299](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-299.md) and [NOTE-294](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-294.md). The structural facts are checks of the published model, not of the authors' prose: contexts are sums of basis projectors, counts are chosen to match rounded frequencies, and the authors call the result a "quantization" of a set-theoretical model. Part I's mark of non-classicality (eq. 19) is met by Boolean projection lattices too, and its lattice structure is supposed, not derived. The model as printed is also infeasible in two cells. It does not say that no quantum model of concepts does better. | Active |
| [THEORY-550](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-550.md) | Clustering is not epistemically superior | Søgaard (2024), [LIT-162](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-162.md), read in [NOTE-108](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-108.md). A rebuttal of two arguments for clustering's superiority, the No-Bias Argument and the Simplicity-Truth Argument, by toy counterexample and by the technical literature on overfitting in unsupervised learning (Hansen & Larsen 1996). The negative claims are firm. The paper's positive step, that supervised classification is "at least as" justified, is under-argued and is not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-562](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-562.md) | REST2 replica mixing doesn't show sampling | Koneru, Reid & Robustelli (2025), [LIT-076](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-076.md), read in full in [NOTE-076](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-076.md). A how-to chapter whose one load-bearing methodological point is that high swap acceptance "is not, in isolation, sufficient evidence of robust conformational sampling or convergence" (p. 18). The reason the reading draws out is that REST2's upper rungs are unphysical Hamiltonians on which disordered chains over-collapse, so replicas can swap freely without the chain rearranging. The chapter argues this and shows a passing example; it shows no failed run, and its convergence criteria have no quantitative threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md) v2 | Model can grow its own structure, unreliably | Smith, Schwartenbeck, Parr and Friston (2020), [LIT-615](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-615.md), read in [NOTE-485](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-485.md). Expansion works in the toy domain over eight runs per condition, and only for novel stimuli. Reduction is the weak half: over 100 runs, the true number of concepts won in 45–80% of runs for four to seven, never for two or three, and in every run when the likelihood was given. Table 1 is the record's only measurement of how often reduction picks the generating structure when the parent model was itself learned. One initialisation; eight concepts, six binary features. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-569](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-569.md) | Coherence explanatory power favours richer sets | Hartmann & Trpin (2026), [LIT-165](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-165.md), read in [NOTE-168](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-168.md), which recomputed all three numerical claims. One theorem (TLI for singleton explanans sets), one counterexample (OLI fails) and two parameterised existence examples (a distal cause for P(H1) < .7; a negatively interacting cause for P(H1) = P(H2) < .75). The escape from Roche & Sober is representational: a set is scored differently from the conjunction, and the two-place theorems still hold for conjunctions. No characterisation says when the richer set wins, and the paper's claim that the measure "accommodates key scientific judgments" is more than the body shows. | Active |
| [THEORY-587](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-587.md) | U-turn stopping keeps HMC exact | Hoffman & Gelman (2011), [LIT-085](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-085.md), read in full in [NOTE-081](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-081.md). The invariance argument (conditions C.1–C.4 and the 2⁻ʲ tree probability) is complete, and so is the O(j)-memory kernel. Ergodicity is not addressed. The efficiency comparison is against HMC with an identity mass matrix on four smooth, near-unimodal targets, and the dual-averaging constants were tuned on one of the four. The account is of the 2011 algorithm; production NUTS has since changed its selection rule, U-turn criterion and adaptation. | Active |
| [THEORY-611](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-611.md) v4 | Guided field may be the gradient of no density | Ho & Salimans (2022), [LIT-839](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-839.md), read in full in [NOTE-603](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-603.md), with the derivations of Section 3 checked line by line. The non-conservativeness argument is credited to Salimans & Ho (2021). The FID–IS trade-off is shown on class-conditional ImageNet only. [NOTE-603](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-603.md) declined a THEORY because the anthology holds the account of what the guidance weight does to metrics; this one states only the probabilistic point, which the record's CLAIM-123 cites as a caveat beyond its thesis and does not use. | Active |
| [THEORY-614](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-614.md) v3 | ICL can be Bayesian inference over concepts | Xie, Raghunathan, Liang & Ma (2021), [LIT-797](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-797.md), read in [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md). Theorem 1 is proved under Assumptions 1–5 and a distinguishability condition; Theorems 2–3 give roughly 1/k excess risk without it. The proofs were not followed in the reading. [NOTE-633](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-633.md) declined a THEORY because the result is conditional on exact fit to a specific generative model, so it is a consequence of that model, not a fact about language models. It is filed Proposed under the owner's ruling, with the condition in the title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-617](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-617.md) | Mutual information's SNR derivative is MMSE/2 | Guo, Shamai & Verdú (2004), [LIT-058](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-058.md), read in full in [NOTE-086](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-086.md). Proved five ways for every finite-power input, in scalar, vector, discrete-time and continuous-time forms. It concerns the optimal, conditional-mean estimator; carrying it to a trained diffusion model's learned denoiser needs the mismatched version, which is later work. Theorems 3, 4 and 11 are stated without proof. | Active |
| [THEORY-696](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-696.md) v2 | Pooling under multiplicative noise boosts growth | Peters & Adamou (2022), [LIT-035](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-035.md), read in [NOTE-059](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-059.md). The mathematics is correct and self-contained, and the paper's own citations show the pooled-variance result was known (McCloskey, Winterhalder, Uitdehaag, Kennedy et al.). Sharing leaves the ensemble rate μ unchanged, so an analysis built on expectations sees no reason to share, and the time average does. It holds with zero cost, perfect pooling, unbreakable pacts and unconstrained growth. It is a sufficient mechanism in that model, not a solution of the cooperation puzzle, and not a showing that cooperation is the default. | Active |
| [THEORY-718](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-718.md) | Evidence is likelihood times an Occam factor | MacKay (1992), [LIT-623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-623.md), Eqs. 5–6 with Eqs. 16 and 19–20, read in [NOTE-471](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-471.md): for y = Φw + noise with Gaussian noise of precision β and the prior w ~ N(0, α⁻¹I) on k weights, the posterior is exactly Gaussian, so the evidence is exactly P(D\|w_MP) times the Occam factor P(w_MP)(2π)^{k/2} det^{-1/2}A, with A = αI + βΦᵀΦ. If ΦᵀΦ/n converges to a positive-definite matrix and w_MP stays bounded, the log Occam factor is −(k/2) log n + O(1). Exact for this model class only. The general regular case and the singular case are [THEORY-087](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-087.md), which is Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-744](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-744.md) v3 | α sets the limit diffusion's invariant density | Coifman and Lafon (2006), [LIT-1246](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1246.md), read in [NOTE-985](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-985.md), with the PNAS announcement [LIT-981](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-981.md). The paper states the limit as a Schrödinger operator. Written as a drift, it shows what each α keeps of the density: the walk's stationary density is q^{2(1−α)}. On a manifold without boundary the limit is derived in full, the kernel expansion included (re-derived on promotion, 2026-10-20). The paper's own α = 1/2 display has a sign error. Its boundary rate and heat-kernel proof are incomplete and are left to [QUESTION-231](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-231.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-762](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-762.md) | Eigenfunctions are memoryless in mean only | The record's answer to what Nadler et al. ([LIT-1250](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1250.md), read in [NOTE-986](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-986.md)) leave implicit when they call slow eigenfunctions reaction coordinates. Such a coordinate is exactly closed in its mean: its best prediction from the full state and from its own history coincide, with no memory term, and the Mori–Zwanzig memory and noise for it vanish under Mori's projection. It is closed in law only under a further condition. In the paper's examples the condition holds; the mixed Ornstein–Uhlenbeck eigenfunction x₁x₂ shows it can fail. This does not say that diffusion maps estimate the eigenfunctions well from finite data, or that a slow eigenfunction is the best coarse variable. | Active |
| [THEORY-769](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-769.md) v2 | Body ownership is causal inference | Apps & Tsakiris (2014), [LIT-1262](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1262.md), read in full in [NOTE-991](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-991.md), with Botvinick & Cohen (1998), [LIT-1277](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1277.md), for the illusion it explains. The rubber hand, enfacement and rubber-voice illusions are read as one inference: unimodal surprise from synchronous stimulation is explained away by shifting the probability that a part is "me". The account fits the findings; its authors grant there is little direct evidence and that it is hard to falsify with standard fMRI. It does not say why such a model is experienced as a self. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-775](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-775.md) | VAE slowness prior gives SFA only when whitened | Schüler and Wiskott (2025), [LIT-1296](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1296.md), read in full in [NOTE-1015](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1015.md). The ELBO of a dynamical VAE with prior N(z_{t−1}, I) and encoder N(g(x_t), I) is Σ E log p(x_t \| z_t) − ½Σ‖g(x_{t−1}) − g(x_t)‖² − (T − 1)d/2, an exact identity. For linear Gaussian encoder and decoder on whitened input, the maximizer spans the bottom eigenvectors of the difference covariance with eigenvalue μ < 1, each scaled by (μ^{−1/2} − 1)^{1/2} and then rotated arbitrarily. So it recovers SFA's slow span, cut at lag-one autocorrelation ½, not SFA's features. On raw input it trades variance against slowness. It says nothing about nonlinear encoders, about predictive sufficiency, or about Turner and Sahani's model. | Active |
| [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) | Meaning depends on what speaker could have said | Frank and Goodman (2012), [LIT-821](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-821.md), and Goodman and Frank's review (2016), [LIT-816](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-816.md), present listener inference as the inversion of an informative speaker, the rational speech act account. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-172](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-172.md), the fits of that model to mean bets in one-shot reference games and Bergen, Goodman and Levy's signalling-game result. This is the mechanism the fits were offered for, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-796](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-796.md) | Question-order effects obey the QQ equality | Wang, Solloway, Shiffrin & Busemeyer (2014), [LIT-795](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-795.md), after Wang & Busemeyer (2013), [LIT-834](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-834.md). The general law the PNAS paper proposes, filed apart from what its 66 Pew surveys and 72 studies measured ([THEORY-166](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-166.md)) under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4. The equality is a symmetry of Lüders projectors and a classical model with order events can meet it, so the law does not by itself favour quantum probability. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-805](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-805.md) | Volume-maximizing SSL's equal-cluster prior hurts | The general reading that [THEORY-306](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-306.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the explicit priors of MSN and SwAV and to one experiment with two to eight classes per batch (batch 033). Assran et al. (2022), [LIT-231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-231.md), read in [NOTE-850](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-850.md), argue the prior for the whole class, VICReg through an informal reduction to K-means and SimCLR through a cited equivalence, and read it as the cause of the degradation reported on real long-tailed data. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-808](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-808.md) | Transformers learn factored belief subspaces | The general reading that [THEORY-256](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-256.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the five Mess3 and Bloch Walk factors and the 4-layer GPT-2-style models tested (batch 019). Shai et al. (2026), [LIT-986](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-986.md), read in [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md), present next-token training (the paper is titled “Transformers learn factored representations”) as yielding factored, orthogonal belief representations; [NOTE-758](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-758.md)'s claims C2 to C4 are each shown on one family of synthetic processes. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. It does not include the paper's inference that the preference is architectural (C5), which App. D.4 leaves open, or the claim that the factored form persists at convergence under strong noise, which Fig. 12 contradicts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-811](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-811.md) | Kernel quantum entropy approximates KL to O(σ²) | The general reading that [THEORY-313](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-313.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the one kernel family on the torus that the rate is shown for. Bach (2022), [LIT-255](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-255.md), read in [NOTE-837](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-837.md), asserts that other translation-invariant kernels and kernels on compact groups behave alike, and sketches a leverage-score argument without completing it. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-816](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-816.md) | Size principle follows from informative speakers | Frank, Goodman, Lai and Tenenbaum (2009), [LIT-824](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-824.md), read in [NOTE-627](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-627.md), derive the size principle from an informative speaker and present the word learner as inverting that speaker. The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-472](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-472.md), the derivation and one experiment in which mean bets matched the inversion; in those displays an informative-speaker learner and a plain size-principle learner coincide, so whether learners reason about the speaker is open. [THEORY-785](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-785.md) is the same inversion for listeners in reference games. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-818](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-818.md) v4 | NARMAX closure doubles Lorenz 96 forecast lead | Chorin and Lu (2015), [LIT-1304](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1304.md), read in [NOTE-1028](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1028.md). A data-driven closure with one or two steps of discrete memory, plus one moving-average innovation, is enough on this test to reproduce the resolved statistics and to double forecast skill against a memoryless-in-x closure. It is the record's first evidence that a short discrete memory suffices in a chaotic system with no scale gap. It is one system, the structure was tuned, and there is no bound, so it does not give the controlled prediction error [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) asks for. | Active |
| [THEORY-819](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-819.md) | Wiener projection removes Mori–Zwanzig memory | Lin and Lu (2021), [LIT-1307](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1307.md), read in [NOTE-1029](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1029.md). Mori–Zwanzig's memory is what a projection onto the present leaves out; a projection onto the whole past absorbs it, leaving the causal Wiener filter on the coarse variable's own history and a residual orthogonal to all of that history. Second-order (linear-span) projections, invertible dynamics and stationarity only. It gives no finite augmentation with a bounded error in general: the NARMAX step is the paper's uncontrolled approximation, exact only in the linear Gaussian class shown here. | Active |
| [THEORY-829](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-829.md) | Ultralarge conjunctions of beliefs can fail | Wenmackers (2011), [LIT-163](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-163.md), Ch. 3 (Stratified Belief, Def. 1; the Stratified Conjunction Principle, Def. 2, eq. 3.5 and §3.6.3.2), read in full in [NOTE-139](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-139.md); re-derived by the promotion audit from finite subadditivity and Hrbacek's Closure principle. A result inside the framework: it says nothing about whether belief has levels, and any explicit level boundary collapses the model back to a fixed threshold. | Active |
| [THEORY-882](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-882.md) v2 | Consciousness requires epistemic depth | Laukkonen, Friston & Chandaria (2025), [LIT-1363](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1363.md), read in full in [NOTE-1063](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1063.md) from PsyArXiv v3. A conceptual proposal with no data and no simulation. The three conditions are asserted necessary; their joint sufficiency is argued for AI and then withdrawn for phenomenal experience in a footnote. The formal part (Table 1) is a hierarchy with layer-wise precision hyper-parameters, from which none of the properties the text gives epistemic depth is derived. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-883](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-883.md) | Conscious contents are policy-informing posteriors | Whyte, Corcoran, Robinson, Smith, Moran, Parr, Friston, Seth & Hohwy (2026), [LIT-1364](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1364.md), read in full in [NOTE-1062](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1062.md) from arXiv v2. The "hard core" the paper reads off the active inference models of rivalry, access, no-report, interoception and meta-awareness. The first two parts follow from the framework; the criterion of access is "an inference to the best explanation" from what the models needed in order to report. The authors scope it to humans and similar animals and are agnostic elsewhere. Neither prediction has been tested in the paper. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-923](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-923.md) v2 | One T-maze run: habits persist after devaluation | Friston, FitzGerald, Rigoli, Schwartenbeck, O'Doherty & Pezzulo (2016), [LIT-1476](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1476.md), read in full from the CC BY version of record in [NOTE-1138](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1138.md). One simulated T-maze task. The habit is one more policy scored by posterior probability; its prior and transitions grow by count, not by reward. It shows persistence under devaluation, a cached mapping failing when what is appropriate changes; it does not show amortization, and its reaction times are simulation run times. | Active |
| [THEORY-937](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-937.md) v2 | Mixture of experts learns faster and specializes | Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan and Hinton (1991), read in full in [NOTE-1147](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1147.md) from a scan of the published article. The gradients of Eqs. 1.4 and 1.5 were re-derived when filed. The task is small (two formants, 75 speakers, 25 runs per system) and has two natural subtasks; the idle experts are read by the authors as economy, and their recovery is not tested. | Active |
| [THEORY-951](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-951.md) | SPRT saves about half of fixed-sample size | Wald (1945), [LIT-1523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1523.md), read in [NOTE-1165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1165.md). The SPRT's operating characteristic and mean sample size follow from two identities of the stopped walk, and its optimality from Jensen's inequality, all exact when the walk stops on the boundary. Optimality with overshoot is only conjectured in the paper. The drift-diffusion limit that the record takes from Bogacz et al. ([LIT-569](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-569.md), [THEORY-068](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-068.md)) is not stated by Wald. It is the case in which his approximations become exact. | Active |
| [THEORY-952](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-952.md) | Wald's boundaries bound SPRT error rates | Wald (1945), [LIT-1523](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1523.md), read in [NOTE-1165](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1165.md). The boundaries of a sequential likelihood-ratio test follow from the error rates by a two-line argument that needs only termination, so the test needs no sampling distribution. The approximate boundaries are conservative in sum. Either error alone may rise, but only by a factor 1/(1 − β) or 1/(1 − α) at most. Nothing here says how many observations the test takes or that it is optimal: that is [THEORY-951](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-951.md), and it needs i.i.d. observations. | Active |
| [THEORY-954](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-954.md) | Bayesian design averages local criteria over prior | Chaloner and Verdinelli (1995), [LIT-1525](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1525.md), read in [NOTE-1161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1161.md). Once the information depends on θ, no design is optimal without saying which θ it is optimal for, and the prior is how that is said. The approximations' accuracy is "not much known" in general. The claim that optimal Bayesian designs gain support points as the prior disperses rests on examples, not a theorem, and is not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-956](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-956.md) | Bayes D- and A-optimality are data-free | Chaloner and Verdinelli (1995), [LIT-1525](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1525.md), read in [NOTE-1161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1161.md). The alphabetical criteria are utilities in disguise, and the utility fixes the criterion. This holds exactly only in the normal linear model with known variance. With unknown variance only Bayes A keeps its simple form, and in nonlinear models the criteria are approximations ([THEORY-954](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-954.md)). E- and G-optimality have no utility behind them. | Active |
| [THEORY-958](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-958.md) | MultiDiffusion step is a per-pixel weighted mean | Bar-Tal, Yariv, Lipman and Dekel (2023), [LIT-1522](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1522.md), read in [NOTE-1158](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1158.md). The fusion is an average, not a sum: where views overlap each takes a convex share of the pixel's update. The paper's closed form is the minimizer of its loss only for 0/1 weights. Its distributional guarantee is conditional on zero loss and, in the proceedings version, on strictly positive weights, so it covers neither the overlaps as they behave nor masked region generation. Nothing here says what distribution the fused sampler targets. | Active |
| [THEORY-960](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-960.md) | DeGroot consensus needs one aperiodic closed class | DeGroot (1974), [LIT-1527](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1527.md), read in [NOTE-1157](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1157.md). Repeated averaging with fixed weights is a Markov chain run on opinions, and whether it ends in agreement is a question about the chain's closed classes and their periods. It is not about how much each member trusts itself. The weights are fixed and no evidence enters, so nothing here says the consensus is right, and the periodic failure is a discrete-time one. | Active |
| [THEORY-969](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-969.md) v2 | hLDA documents draw from a single tree path | Blei, Griffiths and Jordan (2010), [LIT-1542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1542.md), read in [NOTE-1176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1176.md). hLDA's overlap between documents is nested by construction: at each level of the tree the documents are partitioned, and a document can share topics with two others only if one of the two shares all of its shared topics with it. It is a statement about the model, not about the data, and it says nothing about whether the tree the sampler finds is identified. The multiple-path relaxation is the nested HDP's ([LIT-002](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-002.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-972](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-972.md) v2 | Author–topic likelihood is unidentified in basis | Rosen-Zvi, Chemudugunta, Griffiths, Smyth and Steyvers (2010), [LIT-1546](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1546.md), read in [NOTE-1180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1180.md). The likelihood sees members' topic profiles only through the word distributions they jointly produce, and a small change of topic basis that keeps every distribution a distribution produces exactly the same corpus probabilities. Only the Dirichlet priors then choose among the profiles. It says nothing about the posterior's concentration, and nothing about conditions under which Φ and Θ are identified up to permutation. | Active |
| [THEORY-985](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-985.md) v2 | Beta process mixes the Indian buffet process | Thibaux and Jordan (2007), [LIT-1537](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1537.md), read in [NOTE-1171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1171.md). The beta process plays for the IBP the role the Dirichlet process plays for the Chinese restaurant process, and its concentration c separates how much objects share from the mass γ that sets features per object. The conjugacy it rests on is cited, not proved, in the paper. It does not give dependence between features or over time. | Active |
| [THEORY-989](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-989.md) | hLDA beats flat LDA on held-out JACM abstracts | Blei, Griffiths and Jordan (2010), [LIT-1542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1542.md), §6.3 and Fig. 9, read in [NOTE-1176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1176.md). One corpus, five-fold cross-validation, hyperparameters integrated out. It is evidence that a single-path hierarchy can earn its constraint in prediction, near its own size. It is not evidence that a hierarchy predicts better than a flat mixed-membership model in general: the paper itself says the flat model should dominate at large topic counts. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-993](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-993.md) v2 | MMSB memberships are unidentified up to R | Airoldi, Blei, Fienberg and Xing (2008), [LIT-1553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1553.md), read in [NOTE-1179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1179.md). The paper says the blockmodel and the memberships do not compete, because one is global and asymmetric and the other local and symmetric. Given the memberships they do: a change of block basis moves every node's memberships toward the centre and sharpens B, with the same edge probabilities. What can still separate them is the Dirichlet family assumed for memberships, not the graph. The confounding of ρ with B's scale is exact even in the marginal likelihood. | Active |
| [THEORY-999](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-999.md) v3 | Finite beta–Bernoulli undercounts the IBP | Griffiths and Ghahramani (2011), [LIT-1556](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1556.md), read in [NOTE-1172](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1172.md), derive the IBP as the K → ∞ limit of πk ~ Beta(α/K, 1), zik ~ Bernoulli(πk), and give K+ ~ Poisson(αH_N) for the limit only. At finite K the count falls short, by 27% at N = 12, α = 3, K = 16. It says nothing about stick-breaking truncations, which approach the IBP much faster. | Active |
| [THEORY-1003](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1003.md) | Author–topic beats LDA only on short documents | Rosen-Zvi, Chemudugunta, Griffiths, Smyth and Steyvers (2010), [LIT-1546](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1546.md), §6.4 and Fig. 11, read in [NOTE-1180](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1180.md). Pooling by member helps prediction of a document of which little has been seen and costs it once the document's own words are enough. One corpus, one split, one topic count. It is not evidence that member-level structure is real, only that it predicts in a regime of sparse evidence. | Active |
| [THEORY-1006](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1006.md) v2 | dIBP prevalence is constant across covariates | Williamson, Orbanz and Ghahramani (2010), [LIT-1548](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1548.md), read in [NOTE-1175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1175.md). Thresholding at a fixed quantile keeps each feature's prevalence at its stick length at every covariate value, which is what a hand-written logistic transition does not do. The paper's statement that Z(t) is an IBP at each t holds for its collapsed model; with a shared feature-level GP it holds item by item only. Persistence for a fixed correlation still falls with prevalence. | Active |
| [THEORY-1008](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1008.md) | MMSB memberships predict protein function | Airoldi, Blei, Fienberg and Xing (2008), [LIT-1553](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1553.md), §4.3.2 and Figs. 10–12, read in [NOTE-1179](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1179.md). The batch's one check of inferred mixed memberships against labels the model never saw. The reported margin is over a weak baseline, so it shows less than it seems: probably some information, not yet how much. It says nothing about whether the fifteen blocks are the fifteen functions. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1010](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1010.md) v2 | hLDA sampler recovers the true tree in 8 of 10 | Blei, Griffiths and Jordan (2010), [LIT-1542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1542.md), §6.1 and Fig. 6, read in [NOTE-1176](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1176.md). It shows that the sampler can invert hLDA on data hLDA generated, with sparse, well-separated topics. It does not show that the tree is identified in general, or that a tree found in real data was there to be found. One failure is a posterior that prefers the wrong tree, which no better sampler would fix. | Active |
| [THEORY-1012](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1012.md) v2 | Category-shared features never suppress each other | Doshi-Velez and Ghahramani (2009), [LIT-1544](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1544.md), read in [NOTE-1184](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1184.md). Z = f(CM) with f(0) = 0 gives correlated nonparametric feature models with O(log log N) expected features for the DP-IBP and IBP-IBP. The correlations are motifs, sets of features switched on together, plus, in the DP-IBP, exclusion between categories; suppression is outside them, and negative correlation is left as future work. The models' predictive advantage over the IBP is mixed in the paper's own table. | Active |
| [THEORY-1015](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1015.md) v2 | Concentration c_j sets how much groups share | Thibaux and Jordan (2007), [LIT-1537](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1537.md), read in [NOTE-1171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1171.md). The hierarchical beta process B ~ BP(c0, B0), Aj ~ BP(cj, B) gives several groups one unbounded feature library at group-specific prevalences. It treats each object as in one group, exchangeable within it, and has no dynamics; its one experiment, 58% against 50% on a single text split, is suggestive only. | Active |
| [THEORY-1019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1019.md) v2 | Markov IBP rows are not IBP after step one | Van Gael, Teh and Ghahramani (2008), [LIT-1577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1577.md), read in [NOTE-1199](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1199.md). A chain starting off is on at step t with probability a(1 − (b − a)^t)/(1 − b + a). As M → ∞ the a's form a Poisson process of intensity α/a on (0, 1), so E[number on at t] = α ∫₀¹ E_b[(1 − (b − a)^t)/(1 − b + a)] da. That is α at t = 1 and tends to α·E[ln((2 − b)/(1 − b))]. The number of features ever on is still Poisson(αH_T), as the paper says. This concerns the expected count only, not the full row distribution beyond it. | Active |
| [THEORY-1034](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1034.md) v2 | Markov IBP persistence is independent of rarity | Van Gael, Teh and Ghahramani (2008), [LIT-1577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1577.md), read in [NOTE-1199](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1199.md). Each column is a two-state chain from an off state with a_m = P(0 → 1) ~ Beta(α/M, 1) and b_m = P(1 → 1) ~ Beta(γ, δ), independent, and the stick-breaking construction keeps each b paired with its a as an independent draw. Rarity (small a) and persistence (b) are separate per-feature parameters. It does not say that prevalence is held fixed over time, which it is not ([THEORY-1019](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1019.md)), nor how to share the chains across several objects. | Active |
| [THEORY-1037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1037.md) | Beam slicing samples the iHMM without truncation | Van Gael, Saatci, Teh and Ghahramani (2008), [LIT-1622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1622.md), read in [NOTE-1204](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1204.md). u_t ~ Uniform(0, π_{s_{t−1}s_t}) is an auxiliary variable, so sampling u given s and then s given u leaves p(s \| y) invariant; given u, the forward recursion sums only over transitions with π > u_t, of which there are finitely many per row. It says the sampler is exact, not how fast it mixes ([THEORY-1044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1044.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1041.md) | Truncated stick-breaking IBP approaches αH_N | Teh, Görür and Ghahramani (2007), [LIT-1627](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1627.md), read in [NOTE-1210](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1210.md). μ_(k) = ∏_{l≤k} ν_l with ν_l ~ Beta(α, 1). Truncated at K, the expected number of occupied features is Σ_{k≤K} Σ_{j=1}^{N} (−1)^{j+1} C(N, j) (α/(α + j))^k, which sums to αH_N as K → ∞. At N = 12, α = 3: 6.80, 8.97, 9.27 and 9.31 at K = 8, 16, 24 and 32. It concerns the prior's expected count, not a posterior, and the paper itself computes no truncation error. | Active |
| [THEORY-1043](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1043.md) v2 | IBP is the finite feature model's limit | Griffiths and Ghahramani (2005), [LIT-1623](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1623.md), read in [NOTE-1208](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1208.md), and their review ([LIT-1556](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1556.md)). P([Z]) → α^{K+}/∏_{h≥1} K_h! · exp{−αH_N} · ∏_k (N − m_k)!(m_k − 1)!/N! on lof-classes, and the buffet gives the same. It is a statement about the limit: at finite K the expected count of occupied features is below αH_N ([THEORY-999](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-999.md)), and an ordered truncation of the same limit is a different approximation ([THEORY-1041](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1041.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1044](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1044.md) | Beam sampler beats Gibbs for the iHMM | Van Gael, Saatci, Teh and Ghahramani (2008), [LIT-1622](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1622.md), read in [NOTE-1204](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1204.md). Two synthetic designs (an almost cyclic 4-state HMM, length 800, 20 runs; persistent 4-state HMMs with self-transitions to 0.999, length 4000, 60 starts), a well-log series and a text task. The beam sampler is exact by construction ([THEORY-1037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1037.md)); how much faster it mixes is shown only in iterations and by eye. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1045](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1045.md) | Factorial HMMs avoid flat-HMM overfitting | Ghahramani and Jordan (1997), [LIT-1628](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1628.md), read in [NOTE-1203](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1203.md). Four sizes, 15 random parameter sets each, 20 training and 20 test sequences of length 20, four-dimensional, C = 0.0025I, one run per set. In bits per observation over the true model, the K^M-state HMM's test excess is 2.29, 9.81, 11.57 and 175.35; the exact factorial HMM's 1.05, 1.26, 2.51 and 4.49; the structured approximation's 1.04, 0.90, 1.53 and 4.30. It is a result on small synthetic problems the model generated, not on real data or long sequences. | Active |
| [THEORY-1046](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1046.md) | Data favour inactive sources at zero residual | Knowles and Ghahramani (2007), [LIT-1626](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1626.md), read in [NOTE-1209](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1209.md). With y = g x + ε, x ~ N(0, 1), ε ~ N(0, σ_ε² I): ∫ p(y \| x) p(x) dx / p(y \| x = 0) = σ̂ exp{μ̂²/(2σ̂²)}, σ̂² = σ_ε²/(σ_ε² + g′g), μ̂ = g′ε/(σ_ε² + g′g). It is the Gaussian case only; the Laplacian case is the paper's (14), checked the same way. It concerns one data point and one source, with the loading known. | Active |
| [THEORY-1097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1097.md) | No Markov blanket formulation individuates | The wider claim dropped when [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) was narrowed to Friston's 2013 formulation and promoted on 2026-10-27 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4: a narrowing's dropped claims go to Proposed entries). Both critiques argue the general form, and the record holds neither of the later formulations it would have to reach. Its promote_when is [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md)'s own, moved here unchanged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1191](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1191.md) | Active-inference habits persist after devaluation | The wide form [THEORY-923](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-923.md) held before the tenth status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-923](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-923.md), Active, is its evidence. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1242](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1242.md) | Early vision tracks retinal info, losses central | The thesis Geisler's review asserts, filed beside [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md) by the status review of 2026-10-30 ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind 1). [THEORY-336](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-336.md), Active, holds what the review reports; whether the parallel holds is this entry's question, and none of the primary stage-by-stage studies (Geisler 1989; Banks, Geisler and Bennett 1987) is read. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1245](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1245.md) | Recursive EFE makes active inference tree search | The general form of Friston, Da Costa, Hafner, Hesp and Parr (2020), [LIT-577](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-577.md), under [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md)'s old title. It was kept here when the twenty-fourth status review narrowed [THEORY-426](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-426.md) to the paper's runs and promoted it ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md) §3; [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The paper shows the planning claim only in single deterministic runs on a T-maze and an 8 × 8 maze ([NOTE-454](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-454.md), C2). It argues tractability from pruning and sparsity and counts evaluations for one maze (C3). It tries no problem where many outcomes stay plausible, and runs no Bayes-adaptive planner beside it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1253](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1253.md) | Evidence heat capacity is half parameters or RLCT | LaMont & Wiggins (2019), [LIT-1882](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1882.md), read in [NOTE-1481](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1481.md): the learning capacity C = −N²∂_N U and its equipartition values (Table II, eqs. 16–18, 24, 28, 30). Active: the regular entries were checked by differentiation, and the singular case exactly in K = a²b² ([CASE-152](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-152.md)'s model), where C approaches λ = ½ as ½ − 1/log n, not with the O(1/N) error the paper states. The statistical "temperature" is a sample size, so nothing in the dictionary is a physical heat flow. | Active |
| [THEORY-1255](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1255.md) v2 | Constant SGD's stationary law can match posterior | Mandt, Hoffman and Blei (2017, [LIT-1898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1898.md); first in 2016, [LIT-1899](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1899.md)), read in [NOTE-1475](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1475.md) and [NOTE-1473](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1473.md). Under Gaussian, constant gradient noise BBᵀ, the continuous-time limit and a quadratic loss with positive-definite Hessian A, the stationary covariance solves AΣ + ΣA = (ε/S)BBᵀ; the preconditioner (2S/εN)(BBᵀ)⁻¹ makes it the posterior's A⁻¹/N exactly. Checked numerically. Active as a result about that model. It does not cover singular posteriors, several basins or the search phase, and it relates the optimiser's noise scale to sample size, not training time to sample size. | Active |
| [THEORY-1257](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1257.md) v2 | Averaged SGD can match posterior covariance | Mandt, Hoffman and Blei (2017), [LIT-1898](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1898.md), §6 and App. G, read in [NOTE-1475](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1475.md). In their OU model, the mean of T stationary iterates at batch S has covariance A⁻¹BBᵀA⁻¹/(TS) to leading order in 1/(Tελ), whatever the step size or constant preconditioner; under a well-specified regular model (BBᵀ = A) that is A⁻¹/(TS), the Gaussian posterior's covariance for TS observations. Checked against the exact discrete covariance. It is the one place the paper ties examples processed to a sample size, and it is about spread in one basin after equilibration, not about which region dominates. | Active |
| [THEORY-1258](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1258.md) v2 | Fractional SGD model is tempered only regionally | Hennick and De Baerdemacker (2025; ICLR 2026), [LIT-1879](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1879.md), read in [NOTE-1467](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1467.md). Their Lemma 3.3 and Corollary 3.2 show that where a scalar effective diffusion D_ξ is constant, the steady state is exp(−L_m/D_ξ), the posterior at effective sample size 1/D_ξ. That is a temperature, and inside such a region it leaves no room for an accessibility correction. Across regions their own equation's zero-flux state is ∝ exp(−∫∇L/D), set by D along the paths between regions; checked on a double well. Active: the algebra and the counterexample are elementary and checked. It does not say SGD is far from Bayesian across regions, only that the paper does not show it is close. | Active |
| [THEORY-1296](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1296.md) v2 | Deliberation selects from mind-wandering's stream | Metzinger (2017), [LIT-1945](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1945.md), pp. 11–17, read in [NOTE-1496](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1496.md). The "cognitive affordance hypothesis": mind-wandering is "mental sleep-walking" that "sets up the inner world" of candidate mental actions, and frontal control "latch[es] onto the best candidate". Offered as a hypothesis after Clark and Cisek's affordance competition, with no data. The second clause is the chapter's own statement that the data "do not help to decide" what the epistemic agent model does, which takes back the principle the 2015 paper stated. "Best" is not defined, so the hypothesis does not say whether selection is by the candidates' content or by relations that govern them. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1304](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1304.md) | LDA draws a topic per word, a mixture per doc | Blei, Ng and Jordan (2003), [LIT-1948](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1948.md), read in full in [NOTE-1519](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1519.md). Active as a statement of the model's structure, which is definitional and is stated in the text (pp. 996–1001); the variational updates were checked against Appendix A. It does not say LDA fits text well, which rests on perplexity on two corpora, or that its topics are anything beyond devices for representing word distributions, which the authors disclaim. | Active |
| [THEORY-1354](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1354.md) | People learn abstract causal functional forms | Lucas & Griffiths (2010), [LIT-2018](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2018.md), read in full in [NOTE-1543](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1543.md). Five blicket-meter experiments: training that suggests a conjunctive, noisy-disjunctive or deterministic form changes judgments of new objects in an identical test block, and more within a domain than across; a two-parameter sigmoid model fits the mean ratings (r = 0.98–0.99). Proposed: small samples, in-sample fits against rivals that cannot vary between conditions, one reversed prediction, one marginal effect, and no preregistered replication read. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1355](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1355.md) v2 | Extinction is learned as a new latent cause | Gershman, Blei & Niv (2010), [LIT-2011](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2011.md), read in [NOTE-1547](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1547.md). A Chinese restaurant process mixture over trials, inferred online by a particle filter, reproduces acquisition, extinction, ABA and ABC renewal and context-specific latent inhibition in simulation; with the concentration set to zero it reproduces the loss of context-dependence after hippocampal lesions and in young rats. Proposed: the support is qualitative simulation beside replotted data from other labs, with no fitted parameters and no quantitative comparison with rival models. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1356](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1356.md) | People build latent task-sets unprompted | Collins and Frank (2013), [LIT-2012](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2012.md), read in [NOTE-1545](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1545.md). Proposed: positive transfer replicated across the paper's two experiments (N = 33, N = 35) but is modest (t = 2.37, p = .024 in Experiment 1), and the negative-transfer interaction was significant over the whole group only in Experiment 1, a trend in Experiment 2. The EEG follow-up re-analyses Experiment 2's participants, so it is no independent replication. The account is behavioural; it does not say people perform Bayesian inference over task-sets, which the authors disclaim, nor that the Chinese-restaurant reuse prior is what people use, which they leave untested. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1357](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1357.md) v3 | Stroke programs match humans at one-shot letters | Lake, Salakhutdinov & Tenenbaum (2015), [LIT-2009](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2009.md), main text and Supplementary Materials read in [NOTE-1542](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1542.md). BPL erred 3.3% against people's 4.5% on 20-way one-shot classification within 10 held-out Omniglot alphabets; judges identified its productions at 49–59% in four visual Turing tests; lesions without token-level learning to learn or without compositionality erred 11.0% and 14.0% and were easier to detect, while removing the type-level priors left classification at 3.5%. Active as the reported measurements, read with the Supplementary Materials' lesions and controls. Independent replication is QUESTION-446's. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Active |
| [THEORY-1358](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1358.md) | Causal schemas enable one-shot causal learning | Kemp, Goodman & Tenenbaum (2010), [LIT-2008](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2008.md), read in [NOTE-1551](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1551.md). A causal schema, a CRP partition of objects with category-level causal models, features and pairwise interactions, sits above object-level causal Bayes nets; four adult experiments in one paradigm show one-shot and zero-shot causal learning and overruling, matched qualitatively better than two baselines, with two misfits. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1359](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1359.md) | Interventions also seek causal overhypotheses | Jiang & Lucas (2024), [LIT-2014](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2014.md), read in [NOTE-1546](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1546.md) (appendices not read). Two preregistered online blicket experiments. Learners that ignore form information or hold one fixed form barely beat random at predicting interventions; the model that does not transfer edges the full model on average (.059 against .055), while per participant the full model is best for the largest group, whose fitted weights mostly favour form information. Proposed: the transfer clause is the weakest, failing at the group level. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1360](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1360.md) | Observers infer whether cues share a cause | Körding et al. (2007), [LIT-2010](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2010.md), read in full in [NOTE-1541](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1541.md). Proposed: one experiment of the authors' own (19 subjects) and a refit of Wallace et al.'s (2004) published data support it, against forced fusion, segregation, a MAP rule and two interaction priors, but the rule that commits to the more probable structure was not compared and only a split-half check tests held-out prediction. It does not say how the prior over causal structure is learned, that the inference is automatic, or that the model is hierarchical; that word is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1361](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1361.md) | Mind reading is inverting a rational planner | Baker, Jara-Ettinger, Saxe and Tenenbaum (2017), [LIT-2013](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2013.md), read in full in [NOTE-1549](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1549.md). It is a computational-level claim, not an account of the algorithm; it does not say the model is hierarchical, a word that is A's, from the owner's pasted synthesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1362](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1362.md) | HGF updates take the same form at every level | Mathys et al. The Hierarchical Gaussian Filter's update equations for n levels: the same precision-weighted prediction-error form at every level above the first, a value prediction error at level 1 and a volatility prediction error above. Proposed until the updates are re-derived. It says nothing about how close the approximation is to exact inversion, whether the parameters can be recovered, or whether people learn this way. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

Learning a constraint is inference over a hierarchy's higher-level parameters (α, β): low within-category variability of shape is the shape bias. The model reproduces Smith et al.'s first- and second-order generalization qualitatively, with no new experiments, and misses the no-name condition. A derivation with illustrative simulations: closed-form trial-by-trial updates for a three-level hierarchy of volatility, of Rescorla–Wagner form, with a learning rate that is the agent's posterior variance and grows with its volatility estimate, and with per-agent coupling parameters standing for individual differences. Proposed until the updates are re-derived. It says nothing about how close the approximation is to exact inversion, or about whether people learn this way. The wording is the reader's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

It does not say the policy beats approximate dynamic programming, which was not compared, that it holds when ambulances are few relative to demand, where it lost, or that it gives the shortest response times, which it seldom did. The random utility model (RUM) treats aggregate stochastic choice as generated by a population of preference maximizers. The paper adds to active inference's expected free energy an expected information gain over model structures. It computes that gain by Bayesian model reduction over a hypothesis space fixed in advance by symmetry priors (81 rules in a three-ball task), so the agent chooses the observations that best discriminate rules. Smith, Friston and Whyte (2022), Journal of Mathematical Psychology 107, 102632, DOI 10.1016/j.jmp.2021.102632 (open access; PMC8956124). A practical tutorial on discrete-state active inference: building POMDPs, simulating with SPM's routines, Dirichlet learning and its novelty term, the neural process theory, hierarchical models, and fitting models to choices with recoverability checks and Bayesian model comparison. Its running example is an explore–exploit task with a costly hint. There information-seeking fades as Dirichlet counts grow, falls as the preference for the larger win sharpens, and returns after surprises. Larremore, Clauset and Jacobs (2014), arXiv 1403.2933. They formulate a degree-corrected bipartite stochastic block model, in which communities are pure-type groups with the same expected connection pattern to the other side's groups.
